subject: Re: FjordCloud evaluation — transition economics and packaging
messages:

Date: 2027-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FjordCloud evaluation — follow-up and ask

Hi Peter / procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate you carving out time. Peter, per our conversation you mentioned ScaleStream is your incumbent and you have a renewal conversation coming up in early July. To model a realistic counteroffer for your team I need a couple of quick items:

- Current committed ARR and billing cadence (month/quarter/annual)
- Effective per-token or per-hour price for the workloads you've been running (or a sample invoice line)
- Any migration constraints (notice period, data egress windows, preferred migration quarter)
- Compliance asks: do you need an executed NDA + SOC2 report before procurement can evaluate pricing?

If you prefer, drop the procurement details in a reply and I’ll pull together a short two-option offer (migration credit vs multi-year committed discount) with clear TCO and recommended packaging (hosted vs dedicated).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Peter Liu <peter.liu@fjordcloud.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fjordcloud.io
Date: 2027-06-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FjordCloud evaluation — follow-up and ask

Jordan, thanks — quick answers below so your team can model.

- Committed ARR: ~$820k/year (renewal window Q3).
- Billing: annual-ish, but operations prefers quarterly-in-arrears for usage lines.
- Effective unit price: incumbent (ScaleStream) blended effective price ~ $0.0036 / token for our high-throughput embedding + chat baseline (we have detailed billing lines if helpful).
- Notice / migration: 60-day termination notice in contract; we aim to migrate in Q4 if economics align.
- Compliance: procurement needs SOC2 summary and an executed MS Purchase Order + SOW; they will not proceed without SOC2 in hand.

Procurement asked that any counteroffer include an illustrative migration credit and a committed option (24 months) with clear escape clauses for model regressions. I’ve attached a short vendor-comparison they requested — procurement@fjordcloud.io will coordinate.

Peter Liu
Head of Platform, FjordCloud

Laura / Sergio — forwarding details from FjordCloud. They want two things: (1) a migration-credit-led, low-risk path to switch from ScaleStream, and (2) a committed 24-month option that beats incumbent effective price by a meaningful delta while protecting Redwood margin.

My proposed structure (rough sketch):
- Option A (Migration-first, 12mo trial + credit): 12-month hosted plan, no-capacity commitment, $200k one-time migration credit applied against first 6 months of invoices; 10% unit discount vs incumbent effective price for first 12 months; SOC2 + PO required.
- Option B (Committed, 24mo reserved): 24-month reserved pool with 20% committed usage discount vs incumbent; annualized effective price target ~$0.0029 / token; includes one-time transition credit of $75k and a data-migration project SOW option.

Notes/questions:
- Procurement asked for an explicit escape clause for model-quality regressions — we should define an evaluation window and an SLA for quality-based termination credits.
- Need confirmation on whether we can offer both credits + committed discount (stacking) or if we should choose one.

Attachments I plan to include: fjordcloud-ma-plan.xlsx (migration schedule + milestones), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

Sergio — can you sanity-check the numbers and margin impact? Laura — if this looks directionally right I’ll package a one-page comparison and send it back to Peter.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan / Laura — ran a quick model and attached a tightened proposal. Key adjustments:

- Option A (Migration-first): make migration credit $175k (applied over months 1–6) + 12% unit discount first 12 months. This reduces cash exposure while still giving a meaningful first-year delta vs incumbent.
- Option B (Committed 24mo): target effective price of $0.00295 / token with $90k transition credit applied against year 1 invoices. Requires minimum 60% utilization of reserved pool to hold price.
- Margin impact: with the committed option we still preserve ~18% gross margin after OPEX assumptions. Migration-first is lower margin in year 1 but drives upsell potential.

Compliance / procurement asks: I recommend attaching the SOC2 summary and a short SOW template. If procurement wants hard SLAs for quality-based termination, propose a 45-day evaluation window during which FjordCloud can run a defined test-set (we can commit to remediation or a pro-rata credit if we miss quality thresholds).

I’ve attached proposal_v2.pdf and an updated fjordcloud-ma-plan.xlsx draft.

Sergio Alvarez
